mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of 1% or more for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 1% or more for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month periods of INDPRO declines exceeding 1% per month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in consumer sentiment (not available, so use CPIAUCSL as a proxy for inflation uncertainty) above 2% month-over-month signals contractionary policy with rising inflation uncertainty, which increases risk premia and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL month-over-month change > 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL jumps by more than 2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by 5% or more for two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average +5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when HOUST is more than 5% above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (i.e., more people employed and unemployment rate paradoxically rises due to labor force expansion) signals a positive labor market absorption, which boosts consumer spending and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises despite labor force growth (implied by context)
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE rises amid labor force expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) after two consecutive quarters of decline signals a recovery in aggregate demand, which lifts corporate earnings expectations and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 4% YoY).
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rebounds after two quarters of decline AND CPIAUCSL <= 4% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 rebounds after two quarters of decline and CPIAUCSL is below 4% YoY.
